newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks slide, stagnation to grip market.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks slide, stagnation to grip market.

text.p: Most Croatian stocks continued to slide in moderate trade on Wednesday and market participants expected a lasting stagnation with only mild losses for blue chips.

"A pessimistic feeling is prevailing at the market at the moment," said Marko Nikolac of Metroholding brokerage, adding this was mostly due to uncertainty clouding the local elections, scheduled for mid-April.
"But I don't foresee any dramatic losses, since most prices have reached a bottom point below which they are unlikely to fall any further," he said.
"We are more likely to see no trade at all than any significant dives," he added.
Another analyst who requested anonymity said investors were holding back because of president's Franjo Tudjman's poor health, pointing to possible political instability.
"TV pictures broadcast from (Bosnian town of) Mostar where he appeared on Saturday showed he was not doing well at all," he said.
Two of 11 issues that traded rose, six fell and three were flat. Volume was slightly higher at 7,002 shares while turnover almost doubled to four million kuna.
Bigger of the only two gainers, hotelier Suncani Hvar, edged up two kuna to 67 on volume of 190 shares.
Another hotel stock Laguna Porec added 11 kuna to 1,430 on volume of 1,014 shares.

Most active food processor Podravka inched down three kuna to 312, with 2,013 shares sold. Nikolac said he was not optimistic about the further growth of the stock which had recently been given a "buy" recommendation by Austrian Raifeissen Bank.
Fully-listed drugs firm Pliva fell 10 kuna to 420, with 1,108 units sold. Zagrebacka Banka lost seven kuna to 1,825, trading 402 shares.
Top decliner Trgovacka Banka lost 370 kuna to 1,250, trading 50 shares.
